text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Islamist prime minister Necmettin Erbakan says the state cannot support gangs even if they are involved in the fight against the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
- Leaders governing Turkey have not changed in the last 30 years.
- Washington says Greek airspace is six miles. Traditional foes Turkey and Greece regularly quarrel over perceived violation of each other's airspace.
- Erbakan signals for a delay in putting into effect regulations that would impose tax on investment accounts.
- The mandate for Operation Provide Comfort -- the U.S.-led allied airforce based in Turkey to protect Iraqi Kurds from Baghdad -- expires in December.
- A law on the handicapped has been waiting for three years on the dusty shelves of parliament.
- The price of wheat has fallen after state interference to curb the price of bread.
- Only 15 percent of the ancient city of Ephesus, on the Aegean coast, has been excavated and the whole city will only be unearthed after another thousand years.
- The foreign ministry denies having signed a new military deal with Isreal
